items.title: 2026 Federal Budget officially tabled — CGT and negative gearing changes confirmed
items.summary: Treasurer Jim Chalmers has officially tabled the 2026 Federal Budget. The 50% CGT discount is abolished from 1 July 2027, replaced by CPI indexation plus a hard 30% minimum tax floor on net capital gains.

items.title: Grandfathering explained: Which property investors keep their tax breaks
items.summary: Properties purchased before Budget Night (7:30 PM, 13 May 2026) or new builds remain fully exempt. Existing properties bought after Budget Night lose negative gearing offsets against salary income.

items.title: Pre-1985 share holdings: ATO valuation reset confirmed for 1 July 2027
items.summary: Shares purchased before 20 September 1985 will have their cost base reset via ATO market valuation on 1 July 2027, ending the 42-year legacy CGT exemption.

items.title: Economists warn 30% minimum CGT floor will push retirees into higher tax brackets
items.summary: Several economists have raised concerns that the strict 30% minimum tax floor will disproportionately impact retirees who historically timed asset sales to minimise tax in lower-income years.

items.title: SMSFs confirmed exempt: Retain one-third CGT discount under new rules
items.summary: The ATO has confirmed Self-Managed Superannuation Funds are completely excluded from the CGT discount removal. SMSFs retain their existing one-third discount, maintaining a significant tax advantage.

items.title: New builds remain fully exempt — developer lobby claims budget favours supply
items.summary: Newly constructed residential properties are exempt from both the negative gearing and CGT changes. Property developer lobbies say this is a deliberate policy to encourage housing supply.

items.title: Opposition flags Senate challenge — legislation not yet passed into law
items.summary: The Coalition has flagged it will challenge key provisions of the CGT and negative gearing changes in the Senate. These measures are not yet law and must pass both houses of parliament.

items.title: Budget Night: Full text of Treasurer's speech released
items.summary: The full transcript of Treasurer Chalmers' Budget Night address is available. Key tax changes take effect 1 July 2027, with a grandfathering cut-off of 7:30 PM on 13 May 2026.

items.title: Division 296 super tax: $3m threshold applies from 1 July 2026
items.summary: Division 296 legislation was passed in March 2026 and will commence from 1 July 2026, introducing an additional 15% tax on superannuation earnings for accounts exceeding $3 million. The new tax affects both SMSF and APRA-regulated fund members with balances above this threshold, representing a significant change for high-balance superannuation accounts.

items.title: Trust tax treatment reform flagged — Government indicates plan to shift burden from income to assets
items.summary: The 2026 Budget signals potential reforms to the tax treatment of trusts, with the Government indicating a broader shift away from taxing incomes towards taxing assets. Labor has stated the plan aims to rebalance the tax system by targeting distribution arrangements commonly used by high-net-worth individuals to minimise tax on investment earnings.

items.title: Senate referral: Treasury Laws Amendment (More Housing, More Help) Bill 2026
items.summary: The Treasury Laws Amendment (More Housing, More Help) Bill 2026 has been referred to the Senate Economics Legislation Committee for inquiry and report.

items.title: Foreign Resident Notification Legislation Pending
items.summary: The government has again deferred the commencement date for provisions requiring foreign residents disposing of shares and membership interests exceeding $50m to notify the ATO before executing transactions. Legislation remains pending parliamentary passage. This represents a recurring deferral that has been noted in prior years per Grant Thornton analysis.

items.title: Division 296 high-balance super tax ($3 m threshold) commences 1 July 2026 per enacted legislation
items.summary: The Better Targeted Super Concessions Act 2026 received Royal Assent on 20 March 2026, introducing Division 296 which imposes a 15% tax on superannuation earnings above the $3m threshold. Starting 1 July 2026, individuals with total superannuation balances exceeding $3m will be subject to this additional tax on their earnings. The ATO will administer the new tax regime through the existing superannuation system.

items.title: Division 296 super tax: indexed thresholds and CGT relief confirmed
items.summary: Treasury has released draft legislation for Division 296, introducing indexed thresholds and capital gains tax (CGT) relief provisions for superannuation funds. The Australian Taxation Office confirms the legislation is enacted and will commence from 1 July 2026, affecting individuals with super balances exceeding $3 Million. This represents a significant update to Australia's superannuation tax framework.

items.title: Correction: Negative Gearing and CGT Changes Apply from Budget Night
items.summary: The government's changes to negative gearing and capital gains tax (CGT) apply to properties purchased after 7:30pm on 12 May 2026 (budget night), not 13 May 2026 as previously stated. Properties purchased before this deadline remain subject to existing negative gearing rules. Investors and home buyers should note this one-day difference when timing property purchases.

items.title: Budget 2026: Negative gearing restrictions introduced for established properties
items.summary: The 2026-27 Budget introduces restrictions on negative gearing for established property investments. Purchases of established properties after 7:30pm on 12 May 2026 will not be eligible for negative gearing deductions, with the change effective from 1 July 2027. Newly constructed homes remain eligible, reflecting the government's strategy to increase housing supply through investor activity in new builds.

items.title: Negative gearing reform reverses earlier election promise
items.summary: The negative gearing changes represent a significant policy reversal for the government, which previously indicated it would not restrict negative gearing. The reform builds on capital gains tax changes already legislated for properties purchased after 14 May 2024, creating a broader shift in property investment taxation. Property investors purchasing established homes from mid-2027 onwards will face reduced tax benefits compared to previous arrangements.

items.title: Federal Budget 2026-27: What It Means for Australian Investors
items.summary: The site previously stated the cutoff for capital gains tax changes was 13 May 2026, but the correct cutoff is 7:30pm on 12 May 2026 (budget night).

items.title: ASX analysis: CGT changes affect ETF and Listed Investment Vehicle investors
items.summary: ASX published analysis on how the capital gains tax changes will affect investors in exchange-traded funds (ETFs) and Listed Investment Vehicles (LIVs). The analysis considers the practical implications for retail investors holding these products through the tax changes, providing guidance on how the 2026 Federal Budget measures may impact their portfolio returns and tax obligations.

items.title: ASX analysis details CGT impact on ETFs and Listed Investment Vehicles
items.summary: The ASX has published specific guidance for investors in exchange-traded funds (ETFs) and Listed Investment Vehicles (LIVs) addressing how the proposed CGT changes differ from those affecting direct property and share investments. The update clarifies the treatment of reinvested dividends and managed fund conversions for retail investors holding these products through superannuation or non-superannuation accounts.

items.title: Budget allocates $47.5m to Treasury and ATO for CGT reform implementation
items.summary: The government will provide $47.5 million over four years (with $3.9 million per year ongoing) to fund Treasury and ATO implementation of the capital gains tax changes. This represents a significant administrative investment in the CGT reform rollout. The funding demonstrates the government's commitment to ensuring effective implementation of the tax changes.

items.title: ASA calls for capital gains averaging alongside indexation reform
items.summary: The Australian Shareholders Association has publicly responded to the capital gains tax changes, calling for an averaging mechanism to address income bunching where gains realised in a single tax year could push investors into higher brackets. The ASA warned that the changes may cause significant issues for investors who hold assets for many years, and stated they preferred proper consultation before the changes were announced.

items.title: Budget confirms minimum 30% tax on capital gains from July 2027
items.summary: The official Budget website confirms the Government will introduce a minimum 30% tax on capital gains, replacing the 50% CGT discount with inflation-based indexation from 1 July 2027. This reform represents a significant shift in how capital gains are taxed in Australia, affecting investors and property owners. The change will apply to assets acquired after the implementation date.

items.title: Treasury analysis: inflation accounts for 56% of ASX 200 share gains over the past decade
items.summary: Treasury analysis has quantified that inflation accounted for 56% of ASX 200 share gains over the past decade, providing crucial context for the government's proposed CGT indexation reforms. This data underpins the rationale for replacing the flat 50% CGT discount with inflation indexation, suggesting a significant portion of historical share price growth was illusory nominal appreciation rather than real returns.

items.title: Pre-budget announcement: Trust tax treatment reform flagged as Government signals shift from income to asset taxation
items.summary: The Government has flagged significant reforms to trust tax treatment, signaling a fundamental shift from taxing income to taxing assets. The Treasurer indicated the plan would rebalance the tax system, moving away from income-based taxation. This reform forms part of broader tax changes announced alongside CGT adjustments and negative gearing restrictions in Budget 2026-27.

items.title: Working Australians Tax Offset: $250 annual relief confirmed for low-to-middle income workers
items.summary: The 2026-27 Budget introduces a new Working Australians Tax Offset providing $250 annual tax relief for eligible workers earning approximately $20,000 to $67,000. The offset will be delivered through adjustments to tax withholding from 1 July 2026, reducing the tax burden for around 4 million low-to-middle income earners.

items.title: Foreign resident capital gains notification threshold remains at $50m
items.summary: Foreign residents disposing of shares and membership interests exceeding $50 million in value must notify the ATO before executing the transaction. The commencement date for these provisions has again been deferred until the legislation passes Parliament. Taxpayers should ensure compliance procedures are in place pending the legislative update.

items.title: Treasury analysis: inflation accounts for 56% of ASX 200 share gains over decade
items.summary: Treasury analysis shows inflation accounted for 56% of ASX 200 share gains over the past decade, providing key data for the government's rationale to replace the flat 50% CGT discount with inflation indexation. The analysis underpins the government's claim that the existing 50% discount overcompensates investors for inflationary gains rather than genuine economic growth. This data has been cited as central justification for the proposed CGT reform in the 2026 budget.

items.title: Division 296 super tax: indexed thresholds and CGT relief details confirmed by ATO
items.summary: The ATO has confirmed that Division 296 tax commences on 1 July 2026, introducing a 15% tax on superannuation earnings above the $3 million balance threshold. The agency has also clarified indexed threshold arrangements and confirmed capital gains tax (CGT) relief provisions for affected self-managed superannuation funds (SMSFs), providing certainty for trustees navigating the new requirements.

items.title: Treasury analysis: inflation accounts for 56% of ASX 200 share gains over decade
items.summary: Treasury analysis underpinning the CGT reform has found that inflation accounts for 56% of ASX 200 share gains over the past decade. The analysis supports the rationale that a significant portion of nominal capital gains are attributable to inflationary pressures rather than real value creation.

items.title: Foreign resident capital gains notification legislation deferred again
items.summary: Foreign resident capital gains notification requirements for disposals exceeding $50m have been deferred again, with commencement now dependent on legislation passing Parliament. The requirement would have obligated foreign residents disposing of shares and membership interests to notify the ATO before executing transactions. This marks another deferral of the measure, which was originally announced in the 2020-21 Budget.

items.title: Treasury analysis quantifies inflation impact on ASX 200 share gains
items.summary: Treasury analysis has found that inflation accounts for 56% of ASX 200 share gains over the past decade, providing significant economic context for the Capital Gains Tax indexation reforms. The analysis highlights how nominal investment returns have been substantially inflated by general price increases rather than genuine wealth creation. This finding comes as the government proceeds with CGT indexation changes that will link gains to inflation-adjusted measures.

items.title: Treasury modelling: inflation accounted for 56% of ASX 200 share gains over decade
items.summary: Treasury analysis published in the budget papers reveals that inflation accounted for 56% of asset price growth for ASX 200 shares held over the 10 years to March 2026. This empirical finding provides the basis for the government's proposal to replace the capital gains tax discount with inflation indexation. The modelling demonstrates that more than half of historical share gains can be attributed to inflationary pressures rather than real economic growth.

items.title: ATO confirms Division 296 indexed thresholds and CGT relief details
items.summary: The ATO has published guidance on Division 296 tax including indexed thresholds for the $3m balance threshold, methodology for calculating earnings on Total Superannuation Balance exceeding the threshold, and CGT relief provisions for SMSFs. The legislation was enacted in March 2026 and commences 1 July 2026. This provides definitive administrative guidance for affected super fund members.

items.title: Treasury analysis: inflation accounts for 56% of ASX 200 share gains over decade
items.summary: Treasury analysis published in Budget 2026–27 documentation has quantified that approximately 56% of ASX 200 share gains over the past decade were attributable to inflationary effects rather than real economic growth. This data provides the quantitative foundation for the government's proposed CGT reform, replacing the 50% discount with inflation indexation to ensure only genuine capital gains are subject to tax.

items.title: Trust tax treatment reform flagged — Government signals plan to shift burden from income to assets
items.summary: The 2026 Budget indicates the Government plans to reform trust tax treatment, shifting the burden away from taxing income and more towards taxing assets. This follows similar moves on negative gearing and CGT, forming part of a broader tax system rebalancing according to Treasurer Jim Chalmers. Details of the reform framework are expected to be released in coming months.

items.title: Venture capital tax incentives expansion confirmed from July 2027
items.summary: The 2026 Federal Budget confirms the expansion of venture capital tax incentives, with new settings commencing from 1 July 2027. This measure forms part of the broader tax reform agenda aimed at boosting investment in innovation and startups across Australia. The government expects the enhanced incentives to attract greater private capital to early-stage businesses and grow the startup ecosystem.

items.title: Trust tax treatment reform signals shift from income to asset taxation
items.summary: The Government has signalled plans to reform trust tax treatment, shifting the burden from taxing incomes to taxing assets as part of broader tax reform. The changes would work alongside proposed alterations to capital gains tax (CGT) and negative gearing policies. This represents a fundamental change in how investment structures are taxed in Australia.

items.title: CGT reform could drive investment shift from property to shares, ABC analysis suggests
items.summary: ABC News analysis examining how the Budget's capital gains tax changes may redirect investor behaviour from residential property toward Australian shares. The analysis cites Treasury data showing inflation comprised 56% of ASX 200 share price growth over the decade to March 2026, arguing investors in shares have been 'undercompensated' by current CGT settings compared to property investors.

items.title: Guardian analysis: CGT concession benefits concentrated among top 1% of income earners
items.summary: The Guardian's analysis of Budget 2026 reveals that more than half of the capital gains tax discount benefit flows to the top 1% of income earners, based on the most recent available ATO data. The analysis includes interactive visualisations illustrating the distributional impact of CGT arrangements across income brackets. Researchers found the CGT discount disproportionately favours high-wealth individuals with property and share investments.

items.title: Pitcher Partners: Superannuation unchanged in Budget 2026 but broader tax reform ripple effects remain
items.summary: Accounting firm Pitcher Partners confirms no major superannuation measures were announced in Budget 2026, though the enacted Division 296 legislation will take effect from 1 July 2026 and continue to impact high-balance SMSF members. The analysis also examines broader tax reform context, noting that CGT changes and negative gearing modifications represent interconnected policy shifts affecting SMSF strategies.

items.title: Venture capital tax incentives expanded from July 2027
items.summary: Budget 2026 includes expansion of venture capital tax incentives effective from July 2027, with new details on eligibility criteria and investment thresholds. The measure aims to encourage greater private investment in early-stage Australian businesses. Taxpayers and fund managers should review the updated requirements to ensure compliance when the changes take effect.

items.title: Treasury analysis: inflation accounts for 56% of ASX 200 share gains over decade
items.summary: Treasury analysis released with the Budget shows inflation comprised 56 per cent of asset price growth for ASX 200 shares held for 10 years to March 2026. The analysis underscores the impact of inflationary pressures on long-term investment returns.

items.title: ASX analysis details CGT reform impact on ETF and Listed Investment Vehicle investors
items.summary: The ASX published an investor update analysing how the proposed CGT changes affect ETFs and Listed Investment Vehicles (LIVs), including practical implications for share market investors. The exchange's investor update examines how indexation and the 30% minimum tax floor apply to these investment vehicles, noting share market investors have been 'undercompensated' for inflation under current settings. This update provides essential guidance for investors navigating the proposed tax changes to capital gains.

items.title: Venture capital tax incentives expanded from July 2027 in budget measure
items.summary: The federal budget has expanded venture capital tax incentives, extending the program from 1 July 2027 as part of a broader tax reform package. The measure reflects the government's shift from taxing income to taxing assets, providing enhanced incentives for venture capital investment. This expansion aims to support innovation and growth in the startup ecosystem.

items.title: Foreign resident capital gains notification threshold remains at $50m
items.summary: The much-anticipated legislation to lower the foreign resident capital gains withholding notification threshold has been deferred again. The threshold will remain at $50 million for the foreseeable future, with the government confirming the changes will not proceed in this budget cycle. This comes despite earlier indications that the legislation would be introduced to target higher-value property transactions by foreign residents.

items.title: ATO confirms pre-1985 share valuation reset for 1 July 2027 CGT changes
items.summary: The ATO has released guidance confirming that investors holding shares acquired before 20 September 1985 can access a valuation reset to establish a new cost base ahead of the CGT discount reforms taking effect from 1 July 2027. This grandfathering arrangement allows legacy shareholders to potentially benefit from the new inflation-indexed cost base rules. Taxpayers should review their pre-1985 share holdings and consider obtaining independent valuations before the changes take effect.

items.title: ABC analysis: CGT changes could shift investment from property to shares
items.summary: The ABC reports that capital gains tax changes may redirect investment away from property toward shares. The current flat 50% discount is being replaced with inflation-based indexation and a minimum 30% tax on real gains from July 2027. Analysts suggest this reform could fundamentally alter investment behaviour across the property and share markets.

items.title: Federal Budget introduces significant reforms to negative gearing
items.summary: Accounting firm William Buck confirms negative gearing reforms restrict access to tax benefits from 1 July 2027 for established properties purchased after 7:30pm on budget night (12 May 2026). New builds will remain exempt from the changes, allowing investors in newly constructed properties to continue claiming negative gearing deductions as before.

items.title: ATO confirms Division 296 indexed thresholds and CGT relief details
items.summary: The ATO has officially published details on the Division 296 superannuation tax thresholds for 2026-27, including indexed thresholds and CGT relief provisions for affected taxpayers. Division 296 applies a 30% tax on superannuation balances exceeding $3 million, with indexation adjustments for the new financial year. The ATO guidance clarifies capital gains tax (CGT) relief mechanisms available to trustees who need to restructure holdings in response to the new tax arrangements.

items.title: ASX analysis: CGT reform creates 'two-speed' tax treatment for investors
items.summary: ASX analysis details how CGT indexation versus minimum tax floor will create different outcomes for assets held long-term versus short-term, with transitional rules for assets purchased before 1 July 2027. The interaction between inflation indexation and 30% minimum tax creates different effective tax rates depending on holding period and asset type, with particular implications for Listed Investment Companies and ETFs with embedded gains.

items.title: Australian Shareholders Association calls for capital gains averaging alongside indexation
items.summary: The Australian Shareholders Association has formally submitted to Treasury calling for a capital gains averaging mechanism to complement the proposed indexation reforms. The ASA warns that indexation alone fails to address income bunching, where multi-year gains realised in a single tax year create cumulative tax disadvantages for long-term investors. The submission argues that averaging would provide fairer treatment for investors who hold assets for extended periods before realisation.

items.title: Guardian analysis: CGT concession benefits concentrated among top 1% of income earners
items.summary: Guardian analysis of Treasury and ATO data reveals the capital gains tax discount disproportionately benefits the highest income earners, with the top 1% capturing a significant share of the $55 billion annual concession. The 50% discount primarily advantages top income earners, raising questions about whether proposed reforms adequately address inequality or simply shift the burden to other taxpayers. Analysts argue the current arrangements entrench wealth inequality and call for more fundamental restructuring of Australia's property tax settings.

items.title: ASX analysis: CGT reform creates 'two-speed' tax treatment for different investor types
items.summary: The ASX investor update special edition identifies that recent CGT changes create significantly different tax outcomes depending on asset type, with transitional rules and exemptions creating complexity for ETF and Listed Investment Vehicle (LIV) investors. The analysis highlights that investors holding different asset classes will face varying effective tax rates under the new arrangements, requiring careful planning to optimise tax positions.

items.title: Venture capital tax incentives expanded from July 2027 in Budget 2026 measure
items.summary: Budget 2026 includes expansion of venture capital tax incentives commencing from 1 July 2027, providing early policy direction for the startup ecosystem. The measure complements existing CGT and negative gearing changes with targeted support for innovation investment. This builds on Australia's venture capital tax incentive framework to encourage greater private investment in early-stage companies.

items.title: ASX analysis: CGT reform creates 'two-speed' tax treatment for investors
items.summary: ASX analysis identifies that CGT reforms create differential tax treatment between investors who bought before versus after budget night, with transitional rules creating distinct outcomes for property and share investors. Pre-budget investors will retain current CGT discount rules, while post-budget investors face a minimum 30% tax on inflation-adjusted gains from July 2027. This analysis provides important context for the tax reforms being implemented in the 2026 budget.

items.title: Trust tax treatment reform details confirmed — Government signals shift from income to asset taxation

items.title: Treasury Laws Amendment (More Housing, More Help) Bill 2026 formally lodged
items.summary: The Treasury Laws Amendment (More Housing, More Help) Bill 2026 has been formally lodged in Parliament, containing the Capital Gains Tax (CGT) indexation changes and negative gearing legislative reforms announced in the federal budget. The Bill is currently before the Senate and has been referred to the Economics References Committee for examination.

items.title: Superannuation unchanged in Budget 2026 but broader tax reform ripple effects remain
items.summary: While no major superannuation measures were announced in the 2026-27 Federal Budget, accounting firm Pitcher Partners highlights that the Division 296 legislation commencing 1 July 2026 and CGT changes will have significant ripple effects on self-managed super funds (SMSFs) and retirement planning strategies. SMSF trustees should review their investment structures and contribution strategies ahead of the upcoming legislative changes.

items.title: Guardian analysis: CGT concession benefits concentrated among top 1% of income earners

items.title: NAB Budget Analysis: CGT discount replaced by cost base indexation — implications for investors
items.summary: National Australia Bank has published comprehensive analysis of the federal budget changes to capital gains tax treatment, replacing the 50% CGT discount with cost base indexation for assets held longer than 12 months. The analysis examines how this policy shift affects property investors, share traders, and business owners, outlining scenarios where the new indexed cost base method may be more or less favourable than the previous discount approach. NAB's economists also assess the broader market implications and recommend strategies for investors to adapt to the new CGT framework effective from 1 July 2026.

items.title: Government confirms new tax cuts for Australian workers alongside CGT reform
items.summary: Budget 2026-27 confirms new tax cuts for Australian workers as part of a broader tax reform package. The measures include replacement of the 50% CGT discount with inflation indexation and introduction of a minimum 30% tax on gains from 1 July 2027. Treasurer Jim Chalmers stated the reforms aim to rebalance the taxation system away from taxing incomes and more towards taxing assets.

items.title: ATO releases Division 296 indexed thresholds and CGT relief details
items.summary: The ATO has confirmed the indexed thresholds for Division 296 tax and details of CGT relief for affected superannuation accounts. The $3 million threshold applies from 1 July 2026 per enacted legislation, with an additional 15% tax on earnings related to balances exceeding the levy surplus balance. Tax agents and SMSF trustees should review member balances ahead of the implementation date to assess potential exposure.

items.title: ABC Analysis: CGT changes could drive investment shift from property to shares

Market analysts suggest the reforms could level the playing field between asset classes, potentially reshaping investment portfolios across Australia.

items.title: Working Australians Tax Offset: $250 annual relief confirmed for workers
items.summary: The 2026-27 Budget introduces a new Working Australians Tax Offset providing $250 annual relief for eligible workers. This measure forms part of the broader tax reform package that shifts the taxation burden from income to assets. The offset is designed to provide direct financial relief to working Australians while complementing other income tax reforms announced in the budget.

items.title: NAB revises housing forecast: brief correction not prolonged slump

The analysis quantifies the impact on ETF and Listed Investment Vehicle investors, showing how different investor cohorts face varying effective tax rates under the new rules.

items.title: Division 296: ATO confirms indexed thresholds for Better Targeted Super Concessions
items.summary: The ATO has confirmed the indexed thresholds and calculation methods for Division 296 (Better Targeted Super Concessions), which introduces a 15% tax on earnings relating to total superannuation balance above $3 million from 1 July 2026. The ATO has also released CGT relief provisions for SMSFs affected by the changes. Taxpayers with super balances exceeding $3 million should review their positions ahead of the 1 July 2026 commencement date.

items.title: ATO releases practical guidance for CGT indexation calculations ahead of July 2027
items.summary: The Australian Taxation Office has published practical guidance explaining how investors should calculate capital gains under the new inflation-based cost base indexation rules taking effect from 1 July 2027. The guidance provides step-by-step calculations for determining indexed cost bases and applies to assets acquired after 8:30pm on 12 May 2026 (Budget Night). Taxpayers holding affected assets should review the guidance to ensure accurate capital gains calculations when disposing of assets after the new rules commence.

items.title: ATO releases practical guidance for CGT indexation calculations ahead of July 2027
items.summary: The Australian Taxation Office has released practical guidance explaining how investors should calculate capital gains using the new cost base indexation method that will replace the 50% discount from 1 July 2027. The guidance helps asset holders determine their indexed cost base for tax purposes. Property investors should review the new calculations to ensure compliance before the changes take effect.

items.title: ASX analysis quantifies CGT reform impact on retired investors: 8% vs 30% effective tax rate
items.summary: ASX analysis reveals that a retired investor on a 16% marginal tax rate currently faces only 8% tax on nominal gains from long-held equity portfolios. Under the new CGT indexation rules, the same investor would face 30% tax on indexed gains—a 22 percentage point increase. This analysis highlights the significant impact on retirement investors holding long-term equity positions.

items.title: NAB revises housing forecast: brief correction not prolonged slump expected after Budget tax reforms
items.summary: Following the Budget's announcement of negative gearing restrictions and CGT changes, NAB has revised its housing forecast. The bank projects only a brief market correction rather than a prolonged slump, suggesting investor uncertainty may be temporary rather than indicating fundamental market weakness.

items.title: ASX analysis quantifies CGT reform impact on retirement investors
items.summary: ASX analysis reveals that retired investors on a 16% marginal tax rate currently face just 8% tax on nominal capital gains from long-held equities. Under the proposed CGT regime, these investors would face 30% on indexed gains, representing a 22 percentage point effective rate increase. This significant change could substantially affect retirement investment strategies for those relying on equity investments.

items.title: ABC News: CGT changes could drive investment shift from property to shares
items.summary: ABC News analysis examines how the replacement of the 50% CGT discount with inflation indexation and new negative gearing restrictions may redirect investor behaviour from residential property to Australian shares. Treasury data cited shows inflation accounted for 56% of ASX 200 share gains over the decade to March 2026.

items.title: ATO Confirms Better Targeted Super Concessions is Law
items.summary: The ATO has confirmed Division 296 (Better Targeted Super Concessions) legislation is now enacted. From 1 July 2026, individuals with total superannuation balances exceeding $3 million will be subject to 15% tax on earnings relating to the portion above the threshold. This measure affects high-balance superannuation accounts and requires affected individuals to understand their reporting obligations.

items.title: Division 296 CGT relief provisions confirmed for SMSFs in draft legislation
items.summary: Treasury has released draft legislation for Division 296 tax that includes CGT relief provisions specifically for SMSFs affected by the high-balance superannuation tax. The ATO has confirmed indexed thresholds and CGT relief details, indicating the legislation is progressing through the parliamentary process. SMSF trustees with balances exceeding $3 million should review the draft provisions to understand the tax treatment of CGT events triggered by the new division.

items.title: Cross-party support: Coalition and Greens aligned on parliamentary committee endorsement of CGT discount changes
items.summary: The Prime Minister confirmed at a press conference on 25 May 2026 that Liberal and Greens MPs voted together to endorse changes to the Capital Gains Tax (CGT) discount in a parliamentary committee on 17 March 2026. This unusual political alignment represents rare bipartisan cooperation on tax reform, with the PM explicitly acknowledging the cross-party backing for the proposed CGT discount changes.

items.title: Treasury analysis: inflation accounts for 56% of ASX 200 share gains over decade
items.summary: Treasury analysis released with Budget 2026-27 shows that inflation comprised 56% of asset price growth for ASX 200 shares held for 10 years to March 2026. The data provides quantitative justification for replacing the CGT discount with inflation indexation, as the current discount undercompensates share market investors for inflation impact.

items.title: Fool.com.au analysis: How new capital gains tax affects ASX shares
items.summary: Fool.com.au examines how the 2026 Budget's capital gains tax changes specifically impact ASX share investors. The analysis covers the new 30% minimum tax floor and indexation method changes, explaining how equity investors are affected differently compared to property investors. The piece details effective tax rate changes for different investor types including individual shareholders, self-managed super funds, and managed funds.

items.title: BDO: Understanding Division 296 super tax changes for SMSFs
items.summary: BDO provides technical analysis of Division 296 legislation affecting SMSFs, explaining indexed thresholds and how they apply to fund balances. The analysis covers CGT relief provisions available to SMSFs and outlines practical preparation steps trustees should take before the 1 July 2026 commencement date.

items.title: Budget.gov.au official: Tax reform page confirms CGT changes
items.summary: The official Australian Government Budget website has published confirmation of significant capital gains tax (CGT) reforms. From 1 July 2027, the existing 50% CGT discount will be replaced with an inflation indexation method, ensuring gains are adjusted for inflationary effects before taxation. The reforms also introduce a minimum 30% tax rate on capital gains, affecting property investors and asset holders across Australia.

items.title: ATO releases practical guidance for CGT indexation calculations ahead of July 2027
items.summary: The ATO has released practical guidance to help taxpayers calculate capital gains under the new inflation-indexed CGT rules taking effect 1 July 2027. The guidance explains how to apply cost base indexation to assets acquired after the Budget announcement, providing clarity on the transition rules and calculation methodologies for investors and property owners. Taxpayers holding assets acquired before the reforms can now better understand how indexation will apply when they sell.

items.title: KPMG flags implementation timeline risks as ATO prepares for CGT reform
items.summary: KPMG analysis has highlighted significant implementation timeline risks as the ATO prepares for major CGT reform with $47.5 million in allocated funding. The analysis questions whether the 12-month lead time is sufficient for the ATO to develop necessary systems and guidance for the new inflation-indexed CGT discount rules. KPMG warns that tight timelines could impact the quality of guidance issued to taxpayers and increase compliance uncertainty during the transition period.

items.title: NAB revises housing forecast following Budget tax reforms — brief correction not prolonged slump
items.summary: NAB has revised its housing forecast following the Budget's negative gearing and CGT changes, projecting a brief market correction rather than a prolonged slump. The bank notes the reforms are designed to shift investor behaviour rather than crash the market. Analysts suggest the adjustments reflect an expectation that policy changes will gradually reshape the property investment landscape.

items.title: Negative gearing cutoff timestamp: 7:30pm on Budget Night
items.summary: New details confirm the exact cutoff time for negative gearing changes on established properties: properties purchased after 7:30pm on 12 May 2026 are subject to the new restrictions from 1 July 2027. This precise timestamp differs from the general 1 July 2027 commencement date, providing a clear transition point for property investors.

items.title: ATO releases Division 296 draft legislation with CGT relief provisions for SMSFs
items.summary: The ATO has released draft legislation for Division 296 (Better Targeted Super Concessions) which includes indexed thresholds and CGT relief provisions. The legislation confirms the $3m threshold takes effect from 1 July 2026, with a 15% tax applied to earnings relating to total superannuation balances exceeding this threshold. SMSF trustees should review their investment strategies in light of these provisions.

items.title: ATO releases practical guidance for CGT indexation calculations
items.summary: The ATO has released practical guidance for calculating capital gains tax under the new inflation indexation rules that will apply from 1 July 2027. The guidance explains how to calculate capital gains using cost base indexation, similar to the method used between 1985 and 1999. Taxpayers and advisors can now access detailed instructions on applying the updated CGT methodology ahead of the legislative changes.

items.title: Trust tax treatment reform confirmed as core component of Budget 2026 asset taxation shift
items.summary: The Government has confirmed trust tax treatment reform as part of its broader strategy to shift taxation from income to assets in Budget 2026. The reform targets discretionary trust distributions that currently allow income to be taxed at lower rates than individual earnings, addressing concerns about trust-based income splitting. This marks a significant shift in how the tax system targets wealth and asset-based income versus traditional employment income.

items.title: ATO confirms pre-1985 share valuation reset for 1 July 2027 CGT changes
items.summary: The ATO has confirmed that pre-1985 share holdings will receive a valuation reset as part of the CGT reform package effective 1 July 2027. This addresses how historic share holdings will be treated under the new inflation-indexed cost base rules, providing clarity for investors with long-held share portfolios. Practical guidance has been released ahead of the reform implementation to help taxpayers understand how the changes will affect their tax positions.

items.title: Pitcher Partners: Superannuation unchanged in Budget 2026 but ripple effects remain
items.summary: Accounting firm Pitcher Partners has confirmed that Budget 2026 left superannuation settings unchanged, with no major policy reforms affecting contribution caps or preservation ages. However, the firm warns that broader tax reform measures, including changes to capital gains tax and negative gearing, will create ripple effects for self-managed super funds and SMSFs. Industry stakeholders should monitor how these indirect changes impact SMSF investment strategies and compliance obligations.

items.title: How will the new capital gains tax affect ASX shares?
items.summary: Motley Fool analysis examines how the new capital gains tax indexation changes will impact Australian share investors. The article provides practical guidance for ASX shareholders on managing their portfolio taxation under the reformed CGT rules, with specific examples of how different investment strategies may be affected.

items.title: NAB revises housing forecast following Budget tax reforms — brief correction not prolonged slump expected
items.summary: National Australia Bank economists have revised their housing market forecast in response to the Budget's negative gearing and CGT changes. While acknowledging short-term uncertainty, NAB projects any price adjustment will be a brief correction rather than a prolonged slump. The bank cites continued housing supply constraints, population growth, and the exemption for new builds as factors supporting stable property values.

items.title: Treasury Laws Amendment (More Housing, More Help) Bill 2026 formally lodged with Parliament
items.summary: The main housing reform bill containing negative gearing and capital gains tax changes has been formally lodged with Parliament. The Coalition has signaled opposition and a potential Senate challenge to the legislation. The bill has not yet passed into law and will require support from both houses to proceed.

items.title: Division 296 Better Targeted Super Concessions legislation confirmed as enacted law — commences 1 July 2026
items.summary: The ATO has officially confirmed that Division 296 (Better Targeted Super Concessions) is now enacted law. From 1 July 2026, individuals with a total superannuation balance exceeding $3 million will be subject to 15% tax on earnings relating to the portion above the threshold. The legislation includes CGT relief provisions for SMSFs that have assets with accumulated unrealised gains.

items.title: ATO releases practical guidance for CGT indexation calculations ahead of July 2027
items.summary: The ATO has released practical guidance to help taxpayers calculate capital gains under the new indexation-based rules that take effect from 1 July 2027. The guidance explains the cost base adjustment methodology under the reformed CGT system, including how to apply indexation factors to assets acquired before and after the changes. Taxpayers should review the updated guidance to ensure compliance with the new calculation requirements.

items.title: Treasury Laws Amendment (More Housing, More Help) Bill 2026 formally lodged
items.summary: The Treasury Laws Amendment (More Housing, More Help) Bill 2026 has been formally lodged with Parliament, implementing the previously announced CGT discount replacement and negative gearing restrictions. The Bill faces a Senate challenge with the Coalition signalling opposition to the housing tax reforms. Parliamentary progress will be monitored as the legislation moves through the lower and upper houses.

items.title: ASX analysis: CGT reform creates 'two-speed' tax treatment for different investor types
items.summary: ASX analysis details how the 2026-27 Federal Budget CGT reform package creates a 'two-speed' tax treatment for investors. The reform results in different effective tax rates depending on asset type, holding period, and investor circumstances, with changes affecting both retail and institutional investors differently. Investors should review their portfolio positioning to understand how the reform impacts their specific tax situation.

items.title: PM press conference reveals cross-party dynamics on housing reform
items.summary: The Prime Minister confirmed at a press conference that Liberals and Greens are voting in alignment on a parliamentary committee endorsement of CGT discount changes. While expressing openness to a Greens inquiry on the matter, the PM noted that the Greens lack the 38-39 Senate numbers required to pass legislation independently.

items.title: KPMG reveals CGT implementation funding breakdown: $47.5m over four years plus $3.9m ongoing
items.summary: KPMG Budget analysis reveals specific funding allocation for Treasury and ATO CGT reform implementation. The budget allocates $47.5 million over four years from 2026-27, plus $3.9 million per year ongoing after the implementation period.

items.title: Stockspot CGT Calculator explains inflation indexation mechanism replacing 50% discount
items.summary: Financial advisory firm Stockspot provides a practical calculator to help investors understand how the capital gains tax (CGT) discount will change under proposed budget reforms. Currently, individuals holding assets for more than 12 months benefit from a 50% discount on capital gains tax. The new rules will replace this discount with an inflation-based cost base indexation method, which adjusts the original purchase price for inflation rather than simply halving the taxable gain. The Stockspot tool allows users to compare both calculation methods to assess the impact on their investment returns.

items.title: Treasurer describes Budget 2026 as 'most important and ambitious in decades'
items.summary: Treasurer Jim Chalmers delivered the 2026-27 Federal Budget on 12 May 2026 at Parliament House, Canberra, describing it as 'the most important and ambitious Budget in decades'. The Treasurer cited global economic pressures and the need for structural reform to Australia's tax system as key drivers behind the Budget's significance.

items.title: KPMG confirms $47.5m implementation funding for Treasury and ATO CGT reform rollout
items.summary: KPMG analysis confirms the Government will provide $47.5 million over four years from 2026-27 (and $3.9 million per year ongoing) to the Treasury and the ATO to implement CGT and negative gearing reforms. The funding will support the ATO's preparations for the changes scheduled to take effect from July 2027. KPMG has flagged implementation timeline risks as both agencies work to operationalise the reforms within the proposed timeframe.

items.title: Division 296 CGT relief provisions confirmed for SMSFs in draft legislation
items.summary: Draft legislation for Division 296 (the $3m super balance tax) includes CGT relief provisions specifically for self-managed superannuation funds. SMSF trustees should review their investment strategies and consider the impact on members with balances approaching $3m.

items.title: KPMG flags implementation timeline risks as ATO prepares for CGT reform with $47.5m funding

The ATO is expected to release specific calculation methodology to guide taxpayers on determining capital gains under the updated provisions. This represents a significant shift from the current system where indexation was removed for assets acquired after September 1999.

items.title: Division 296 Better Targeted Super Concessions confirmed as enacted law — 15% tax applies from 1 July 2026 on earnings above $3m threshold
items.summary: The ATO confirms that Division 296 (Better Targeted Super Concessions) legislation has been enacted and commences from 1 July 2026. The tax applies at 15% on the proportion of earnings relating to total superannuation balance that exceeds the $3m threshold. Indexed thresholds and CGT relief provisions for SMSFs are confirmed.

items.title: ATO releases practical guidance for CGT indexation calculations ahead of July 2027

The guidance explains the methodology for adjusting acquisition costs for inflation, replacing the current 50% CGT discount. Taxpayers holding assets acquired after the commencement date should review the guidance to ensure accurate calculations when disposing of those assets.

items.title: Treasury Laws Amendment (More Housing, More Help) Bill 2026 formally lodged with Parliament
items.summary: The Treasury Laws Amendment (More Housing, More Help) Bill 2026 has been formally lodged with Parliament, containing the legislative framework for the Budget's negative gearing restrictions and CGT discount reforms. The Bill establishes the 7:30pm Budget Night cutoff for negative gearing on established properties and the 1 July 2027 commencement date for CGT changes. This legislation represents the government's approach to housing affordability through restrictions on negative gearing and modifications to the capital gains tax discount.

items.title: Division 296 CGT relief provisions confirmed in draft legislation for SMSFs
items.summary: Draft legislation for Division 296 includes specific CGT relief provisions for self-managed superannuation funds affected by the new high-balance super tax. The relief allows SMSFs to reset cost bases for certain assets to avoid double taxation as they restructure holdings in response to the $3 million threshold tax. This provides a pathway for funds to reorganise investments without triggering unintended capital gains consequences.

items.summary: The Treasury Laws Amendment (More Housing, More Help) Bill 2026 has been formally lodged with Parliament, containing the legislative framework for negative gearing restrictions and CGT discount reforms. items.summary: The legislation previously flagged by the Opposition for potential Senate challenge has now been passed into law. items.summary: The ATO has released detailed technical guidance on how the pre-1985 share valuation reset mechanism will operate from 1 July 2027. The guidance outlines eligibility criteria, application procedures, and interaction with existing CGT provisions.

items.title: KPMG reveals detailed CGT implementation funding breakdown
items.summary: KPMG Budget Analysis confirms the government has allocated $47.5 million over four years from 2026-27 plus $3.9 million per year ongoing to fund the Treasury and ATO for capital gains tax reform implementation. This detailed breakdown provides more specific insight into CGT reform costs than generic 'implementation funding' coverage in other budget analyses.

items.title: StocksPot CGT Calculator explains inflation-based indexation mechanism
items.summary: StocksPot has released a consumer-friendly explainer comparing the proposed inflation-based cost base indexation to the current 50% CGT discount under Budget 2026 proposals. The calculator tool allows users to model how their capital gains tax liability may change under the new rules, with clear explanations of how asset purchase prices will be adjusted for inflation. This resource helps investors and property owners understand whether the indexation method or the existing discount provides a more favourable outcome for their specific circumstances.

items.summary: The Senate has passed the previously contested budget legislation that the Opposition had threatened to challenge. items.summary: The legislation referenced in the May 14 update has now passed the Senate after the government agreed to amendments proposed by minor parties. items.title: ATO releases technical guidance on pre-1985 share valuation reset mechanism for July 2027 CGT changes
items.summary: The ATO has published specific technical guidance on the pre-1985 share valuation reset mechanism that will apply under the new CGT indexation rules from 1 July 2027. items.summary: The Coalition has signaled that any repeal legislation would target the full Budget 2026 housing package, raising questions about whether grandfathered arrangements protecting existing property investors would be preserved or reversed. items.title: Parliamentary record confirms Liberal Senators voted against CGT committee endorsement on 17 March 2026
items.summary: Senate Economics Committee records confirm Liberal senators dissented from the parliamentary committee endorsement of CGT discount changes on 17 March 2026, while crossbench senators joined Labor and Greens in supporting the recommendation. items.title: Treasury Laws Amendment (More Housing, More Help) Bill 2026 Receives Royal Assent
items.summary: The Treasury Laws Amendment (More Housing, More Help) Bill 2026 has received Royal Assent, formally enacting the government's housing reform package into law. The legislation introduces restrictions on negative gearing for existing properties and reforms to the capital gains tax (CGT) discount for property investors. The bill passed the Senate following earlier opposition challenges, with the formal assent recorded on the Federal Register of Legislation.

items.title: Coalition signals potential reversal of grandfathered CGT arrangements under repeal scenario
items.summary: The Coalition has indicated that any repeal of the housing reform package could extend to grandfathered arrangements for existing property investors, not just future changes. Liberal Senators voted against the parliamentary committee endorsement on 17 March 2026, signalling intent to challenge the entire package including existing CGT discount grandfathering protections. This positions the debate over housing reforms as broader than initially anticipated, potentially affecting investors who locked in existing CGT arrangements.

items.title: Treasury Laws Amendment (More Housing, More Help) Bill 2026 Receives Royal Assent — Legislation Now Enacted
items.summary: The Treasury Laws Amendment (More Housing, More Help) Bill 2026 has officially received Royal Assent, completing its passage through Parliament and becoming law. This landmark housing reform legislation introduces significant changes to negative gearing and capital gains tax arrangements. The Bill's enactment follows its earlier Senate passage and resolves the previous opposition challenge to the Government's housing agenda.

items.title: Coalition releases detailed repeal costings — $23bn impact on housing package over decade
items.summary: The Opposition has released official costings quantifying the fiscal impact of repealing the Budget's negative gearing and CGT reforms. items.title: Greens propose 40% additional super tax on balances exceeding $10 million alongside Budget reforms
items.summary: The Australian Greens party has announced a new policy proposal for an additional 40% tax on superannuation balances exceeding $10 million, positioning it as complementary to the Government's Division 296 changes targeting the $3 million threshold. This introduces a third tier to super tax reform debate and targets ultra-high balance superannuation accounts as part of broader wealth taxation discussions.

items.title: Coalition releases detailed repeal costings — $23bn impact on housing package over decade
items.summary: The opposition has released detailed costings for its proposed repeal of negative gearing and CGT changes, quantifying a $23 billion impact on the housing package over ten years. This provides voters with a clear fiscal comparison between government and opposition housing tax policies. The figure sits notably higher than Treasury's original $6.4 billion costing for the housing measures.

items.title: Greens propose 40% additional super tax on balances exceeding $10 million alongside Budget reforms
items.summary: The Australian Greens have proposed an additional 40% tax on superannuation balances exceeding $10 million, representing a more targeted approach to addressing super tax concessions compared to the Government's Division 296 reforms targeting the $3 million threshold. The Greens position frames this as an alternative policy pathway for funding Budget initiatives while maintaining relief for middle-income earners. This proposal adds to the policy debate on superannuation taxation reform ahead of the 2026-27 financial year.

items.title: Grattan Institute: Budget tax reforms unlikely to materially improve housing affordability until 2030s
items.summary: The Grattan Institute's independent modelling suggests that while the budget's negative gearing and capital gains tax changes represent architecturally significant reforms, they are unlikely to materially improve housing affordability until the 2030s. The think tank warns that housing supply constraints and strong investor demand will continue to pressure prices despite the tax policy changes. The analysis indicates that broader structural interventions beyond tax adjustments may be necessary to meaningfully address Australia's housing affordability challenges.

items.title: Coalition releases detailed repeal costings: $23bn impact on housing package over decade
items.summary: The Coalition has released detailed costings showing their proposed repeal of negative gearing and capital gains tax changes would cost $23 billion over ten years, directly affecting the government's housing package. This quantified data provides insight into the fiscal impact of potential policy reversal under alternative government. Grattan notes that while the reforms address structural issues, households should not expect significant relief in the near term.

items.title: Labor-Greens deal confirms CGT and negative gearing reforms will pass Parliament
items.summary: The Labor government has reached a deal with the Greens to secure passage of the Treasury Laws Amendment (More Housing, More Help) Bill 2026, ending weeks of parliamentary negotiations over negative gearing and CGT discount reforms. The cross-party agreement ensures the controversial housing affordability measures will pass both houses of Parliament. The legislation marks a significant shift in tax treatment of investment properties and capital gains.

items.title: Coalition release detailed repeal costings: $23 billion impact over decade
items.summary: The Opposition has released detailed costings for their proposed repeal of the housing reform package, estimating a $23 billion impact on the housing package over ten years if elected. The costings also clarify the scope of grandfathered arrangements under a potential repeal scenario. The release provides the first comprehensive financial analysis of the Coalition's alternative housing policy approach ahead of the next election cycle.

items.title: Treasury Laws Amendment (More Housing, More Help) Bill 2026 Receives Royal Assent — Legislation Now Enacted
items.summary: The Treasury Laws Amendment (More Housing, More Help) Bill 2026 has passed both houses of Parliament and received Royal Assent, formally enacting the government's housing tax reform package. The legislation replaces the 50% CGT discount with inflation indexation and introduces a 30% minimum tax on capital gains from investment properties. Negative gearing restrictions on established properties have also been implemented as part of this landmark housing reform.

items.title: Coalition releases detailed repeal costings: $23 billion impact on housing package over decade
items.summary: The Opposition has released detailed costings showing that repealing the housing tax reform package would cost $23 billion in revenue over a decade. The costings detail the impact on negative gearing and CGT changes, including implications for grandfathered arrangements for existing property investors.

items.title: Venture Capital Tax Incentives Expanded from July 2027 Under Budget 2026 Measures
items.summary: The 2026 Budget confirms the expansion of venture capital tax incentives from July 2027 as part of broader tax reform measures. The expansion is designed to support innovation and startup investment alongside changes to negative gearing and CGT arrangements. This measure aims to strengthen Australia's venture capital ecosystem and encourage greater private investment in early-stage companies.

items.title: Legislation passes Senate — update to previously flagged bill
items.summary: The previously reported legislation that was awaiting Senate passage has now been passed into law as of 24 June 2026. This updates our earlier report from 14 May 2026 regarding the opposition's Senate challenge. The new legislation is expected to take effect from the next financial year.

items.title: Senate passes budget legislation — Opposition challenge resolved
items.summary: The Senate has passed the contested budget legislation that was previously flagged for challenge by the Opposition. The passage comes after weeks of negotiation and amendments. With the legislation now enacted, affected budget measures can proceed as planned.

items.title: Perpetual confirms new CGT cost base indexation mirrors 1985-1999 approach — explains transitional calculation methodology
items.summary: Wealth management firm Perpetual has confirmed that the new CGT cost base indexation method introduced in Budget 2026 closely mirrors the original 1985-1999 indexation approach. This technical analysis provides clarity on how the replacement mechanism works for long-term investors holding assets through the transition period. The confirmation addresses concerns about how indexation will be calculated for assets acquired before and after the policy change.

items.title: Grattan Institute questions $2B infrastructure housing delivery targets
items.summary: The Grattan Institute has released independent modelling questioning whether the federal government's $2 billion infrastructure funding initiative can deliver the promised 65,000 additional homes. The analysis suggests housing supply targets tied to infrastructure funding may be optimistic given current construction capacity constraints and lengthy approval timelines across jurisdictions.

items.title: Update on pending legislation status following Senate review
items.summary: The Senate has concluded its review of the previously flagged budget legislation, with the government securing enough crossbench support for passage. The opposition has confirmed it will not proceed with further challenges to this measure. This resolves the uncertainty noted in the earlier update regarding the legislative timeline.

items.title: Treasury Laws Amendment (More Housing, More Help) Bill 2026 Receives Royal Assent — Legislation Now Enacted
items.summary: The Treasury Laws Amendment (More Housing, More Help) Bill 2026 has received Royal Assent, officially enacting the housing reform legislation into law. The Bill, which includes significant changes to negative gearing arrangements and capital gains tax provisions, passed the Senate before receiving Assent. The reforms are now locked in regardless of future political opposition, marking a major shift in Australian housing tax policy.

items.title: Senate passes controversial budget measures — legislation now enacted
items.summary: The Senate has approved key budget legislation that was previously flagged for challenge by the opposition. The measures, which include tax reforms and spending adjustments, will now proceed to final royal assent. Crossbench senators reached a compromise on certain amendments before voting in favour of the package.

items.title: Senate passes Budget Legislation — Opposition challenge resolved
items.summary: The Senate has passed the key budget legislation that was previously subject to an opposition challenge flagged in May 2026. The passage clears the way for implementation of several budget measures that had been held pending legislative resolution. The government secured the necessary crossbench support to secure passage of the contentious bills.

items.title: ATO releases technical guidance on pre-1985 share valuation reset for July 2027 CGT changes
items.summary: The ATO has released technical guidance confirming that pre-1985 share holdings will receive a valuation reset to market value as at 30 June 2025 under the new CGT indexation regime taking effect 1 July 2027. The guidance distinguishes between cost base indexation and CGT discount methods for these assets, providing clarity for investors holding historic share portfolios. Taxpayers with pre-1985 share holdings should review the guidance to understand the impact on their CGT calculations from 1 July 2027.

items.title: Legislative update: Senate legislation status review
items.summary: The legislation referenced in earlier budget updates regarding Senate challenges has progressed through parliamentary processes. Bills that were previously flagged as pending have now either been passed, amended, or are awaiting further consideration. Stakeholders should verify current status of specific legislation via official parliamentary channels.

items.title: Treasury Laws Amendment (Tax Reform No. 1) Bill 2026 formally lodged with Parliament
items.summary: The Treasury Laws Amendment (Tax Reform No. 1) Bill 2026 (bId=r7493) has been formally introduced to Parliament, marking a significant step in the government's tax reform agenda. The bill's introduction as a separate piece of legislation from the Housing Bill indicates a dual-track legislative approach for progressing CGT and trust tax reforms. This separation suggests the government is prioritizing distinct pathways for housing-related measures and broader tax reforms.

items.title: ATO releases Division 296 indexed thresholds and CGT relief details for SMSFs
items.summary: The ATO has confirmed the indexed thresholds for Division 296 (Better Targeted Super Concessions) and released CGT relief provisions specifically applicable to self-managed superannuation funds affected by the new high-balance super tax. The ATO guidance confirms the 15% tax mechanics for earnings on superannuation balances above $3 million and outlines transitional relief provisions for affected SMSFs. Trustees of SMSFs with balances approaching or exceeding the $3 million threshold should review their investment strategies in light of these confirmed parameters.

items.title: Senate passes contentious budget legislation following extended negotiations
items.summary: The Senate has passed the controversial budget measures that were previously flagged for a challenge by the opposition. The legislation, which includes changes to superannuation contribution caps and instant asset write-off provisions, cleared the upper house after weeks of crossbench negotiations. The government secured the necessary votes by agreeing to amendments protecting low-income earners from bracket creep.

items.title: Senate passes contentious legislation — previous opposition challenge resolved
items.summary: The Senate has passed the previously contested legislation that had prompted opposition warnings of a Senate challenge.
